title: CPU meter menu
contract: The Control Bar CPU meter menu opens via its triangle or meter context click. Menu choices are public control roles; no numeric measurement or scheduler behavior is established.

title: Average Current and off choices
contract: The CPU meter can display Average, Current (peak), or be switched off. Average is documented enabled by default; this is a current-chapter default, not observed target factory state. What exact load each mode measures remains an open source-context question.

title: Combined meter presentation
contract: With Average and Current both enabled, both appear in the menu; the meter uses lighter/darker theme-dependent shades to distinguish the two. No fixed RGB, pixel, numeric averaging window or OS-total meaning is implied.

title: Meter Text Shows selection
contract: Only one of the Average/Current percentage values is shown as meter text at a time; Meter Text Shows selects which. Numeric percentage and refresh timing are ungraded.

title: Shared CPU warning controls
contract: Warn on Current CPU Overload in the CPU menu and CPU Overload Indicator in the Overload context menu share state. Enabling one enables the other; warnings are documented off by default, with exact-target default and thresholds unknown.

title: Performance Impact visibility
contract: Mixer Performance Impact indicators can be enabled via Show/Hide Mixer Config or View Mixer Controls. This specifies public visibility entry points, not CPU calibration.

title: Six-part track impact display
contract: Each track Performance Impact indicator has six rectangles lighting left to right for relative track impact. Level boundaries, detector, timing and track-to-track cost ratios are unknown.

title: Unused I/O selection context
contract: Input/Output Config settings let users disable unused channels; the source says unused channels are not automatically disabled. Availability of actual channels retains the routing/settings owner, and no glitch or performance outcome follows.

title: Disk overload indicator role
contract: The Control Bar Overload indicator presents Disk for a disk read/write load issue. Exact trigger, detector, hold/reset behavior and processing capacity are unknown.

title: CPU overload warning role
contract: With CPU warnings enabled, the Overload indicator presents CPU for processor overload. Indicator appearance does not define a current-load threshold, sample deadline or audio dropout result.

title: Overload audio caveat
contract: The source describes disk/CPU load issues as potentially causing playback/recording dropouts or crackles. This is a conditional caveat, not guaranteed failure at a displayed value or a real-time capacity promise.
source_claim: Disk and CPU load issues can cause audible dropouts/crackles; no detection or failure threshold is supplied.

title: MIDI monitoring context
contract: The MIDI fact sheet distinguishes recording while hearing a direct hardware device from playthrough and describes monitoring-related added latency to record what is heard. Existing recording/routing owners keep Monitor/arm gates and latency options; no timestamp correction, buffer arithmetic or universal mode policy is added.
source_claim: The chapter describes added monitoring latency for MIDI playthrough/recording and recommends monitoring off for direct-hardware listening or device-generated MIDI; exact target interaction with current monitoring options is unknown.

title: MIDI reception during audio dropout
contract: The MIDI fact sheet says incoming MIDI reception/recording should continue through high-load audio dropouts, while playthrough may have timing errors/distortion and later playback should recover. This supplies no loss bound, timing accuracy or required recovery deadline.
source_claim: Publisher prose describes continuing incoming MIDI recording during audio dropouts and accurate later playback after recovery; no retained target event trace or output exists.

title: CPU numeric and source-context outcomes
contract: RES-B011 audio-processing-only wording and RES-B013 total-current wording do not settle Current scope. Ratio formula, averaging/current windows, numeric thresholds, sample-cost, OS CPU, thread/core scheduling and CPU/disk capacity remain unknown.
source_claim: The source explains a processing-buffer-time ratio and gives an example, audio-only scope and total-current wording; these are not a calibrated numeric or scheduling oracle.

title: Conditional undithered render comparison
contract: Undithered render neutrality/bit-depth comparisons require independently retained finite inputs, explicit matching rates and no other processing under the existing export owner. No phase-cancellation, distortion minimum, dither or file oracle is supplied here.
source_claim: The publisher reports cancellation for unprocessed matched-rate rendering to same/higher bit depth and minimal distortion for lower depth under its methodology; no source test data or target results are retained.

title: Matched-rate playback comparison
contract: Unstretched same-rate untransposed playback comparison stays with playback/Clip View owners and excludes the hardware output stage. No broadened reconstruction identity, sample rounding, format or tolerance is established.
source_claim: The fact sheet describes neutral playback for unstretched matching-rate untransposed files before audio hardware, verified by publisher cancellation tests.

title: Conditional Warp and groove comparison
contract: Identity-tempo Warp, tempo return/automation, mode and groove comparisons retain Warp/groove owners. No universal neutrality/non-neutral inequality for all inputs or DSP algorithm is inferred.
source_claim: The publisher describes unstretched Beats/Tones/Texture/Re-Pitch neutrality, mode/tempo-automation caveats and non-neutral Complex/groove processing. Silence, identity settings and other conditions cannot prove a universal difference.

title: Mix-point comparison
contract: Single/multiple mix-point numerical comparison retains mix/rack owners. Source 64-bit summing and 32-bit internal explanations are research context, not required candidate architecture, precision or associativity.
source_claim: Publisher phase-cancellation tests describe single-point summing; its precision/architecture narrative and possible multi-point differences supply no new numeric tolerance or target output.

title: External and internal recording comparison
contract: Bit-depth-conditioned external/internal recording neutrality stays with recording/routing/export owners. Actual A/D/source representation, accepted format, stage and retained results are required; no new recording codec, capacity or bit-exactness rule follows.
source_claim: The fact sheet conditions external recording on source-converter depth and internal recording on 32-bit or unprocessed matching lower depth; it does not supply target capture files or hardware calibration.

title: Additional Freeze fact-sheet contexts
contract: Freeze comparison and generated-file inspection retain the sealed Bounce/Freeze owner. The additional source descriptions of 32-bit files, Arrangement automation, Session values at Arrangement1.1.1, Beats/Warp and fixed random realization remain unverified context, not new target laws. The existing two-cycle role is not duplicated here.
source_claim: Audio fact-sheet Freeze descriptions include file depth, tails/transport, Arrangement versus Session automation snapshot, Warp/Beats playback and rendered randomness. Their exact version/control/automation context needs evidence; existing frozen contracts remain unchanged.

title: Bypass comparison and latency context
contract: Bypass comparison retains common device/host and compensation owners. Source identity and retained-device-delay wording do not establish zero-latency equality, universal bypass tails, reactivation or a new graph/DSP law.
source_claim: The source describes bypassed signal identity but delay retention for delay-requiring devices; cancellation/alignment context and actual output are not retained.

title: Routing source-tap comparison
contract: Routing neutrality comparison uses the selected source tap and destination under the existing routing/mix/Impulse owners. Pre/post-processing taps must not be compared against a different source-stage output as if identical.
source_claim: The fact sheet calls routing neutral while warning source taps can precede processing/mixer or individual instrument outputs; this is no universal end-to-end identity law.

title: Split comparison
contract: Already-neutral clip split comparison retains Arrangement/Clip View/playback owners. Source unwarped-loop examples, seamless/sample-accurate prose and cancellation reports do not override current loop eligibility or provide a boundary/sample oracle.
source_claim: The publisher describes neutral splits and tests including loop-on/off unstretched/unwarped cases. Current Clip View unwarped-loop eligibility is a distinct source context requiring reconciliation, not silent owner expansion.

title: Consolidation file and normalization context
contract: Consolidation stays Arrangement-owned. Source normalization/compensating clip-level and configured rate/depth descriptions remain unverified file/signal context, not new output-header or normalization laws in this packet.
source_claim: The fact sheet says consolidation creates normalized configured-rate/depth files with adjusted clip volume; no generated file, field transform, normalization algorithm or numerical playback equality is supplied.

title: Processing comparison families
contract: SRC/transposition, volume automation, dither, fades, panning and grooves stay with existing owners. Non-neutral classifications identify comparison dimensions, not a proof every input/output differs, a new metric, per-sample update law, required library or architecture.
source_claim: Source descriptions include SoX, internal depth, per-sample volume updates, pan curves and fade/SRC/dither/groove neutrality classifications; existing finite numeric owners and their assumptions remain unchanged.

title: MIDI timing and publisher-report comparison
contract: MIDI timing, monitoring/driver scheduling, serial transport, hardware scan and high-load recording comparisons require known accepted actual sources and clocks. Ideal-system and anonymous A/B/C historical tests provide no zero-jitter promise, target tolerance or current hardware proof.
source_claim: The publisher describes timestamps, monitoring latency, MME scheduling and an anonymous36-configuration A/B/C report with roughly ±1 through ±11ms observations. These are historical reported configurations, not project measurements or acceptance bounds.

title: Control and engine lifecycle
contract: Undo/cancel, persistence/restart, transport/record/automation interactions, rate/block/output changes, unsupported controls, malformed admitted inputs, concurrent engine operations and teardown remain unknown.

title: Resource and source failure
contract: Source/device/port/disk loss, sustained load, memory/CPU/storage limits, overload trigger/recovery/cleanup, dropped MIDI/audio and fallback have no calibrated detector, timeout, silence, event-loss or repair oracle.
